answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a spiral tag. The harbor cap is applied at intake and willow makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a farm in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because each member consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 21 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
